Don't you think you could have found the girl of your dreams eventually?

Present Perfect Continuous vs. Present Perfect

You use these tenses to talk about a past action that is connected to the present in some way. You can use them both to talk about a past action that continues to the present. However, it is more common to use the Present Perfect tense to express that an action is recently completed or to emphasize the result. You use the Present Perfect Continuous tense to emphasize the duration or continuous course of an action.
Ann: I think I'm done with online dating. In fact, I haven't checked my profile in a few weeks.
Bob: Of course, you've always been a bit slow on the uptake.

images.text:
Peter: Hey Mike. I need your expert advice.
Mike: What's going on, buddy? Have you joined another online dating website?
Peter: No. I think I'm done with that. In fact, I haven't checked my profile in a few weeks. It just wasn't for me.
Mike: Don't you think you could've found the girl of your dreams eventually?
Peter: Maybe ... or maybe she's been waiting for me to call her all along.
Mike: What do you mean?

Peter: I've been thinking about this girl I met in college. Her name's Camilla. Sally keeps telling me that she's always had a thing for me, but I was too oblivious to notice she liked me.
Mike: Of course, you've always been a bit slow on the uptake when it comes to girls.
Peter: Very funny ...
Mike: Anyway, how can I help?
Peter: I'd like to ask Camilla out, but I'm worried that she'll find me dull and uninteresting. In fact, I've been trying to change my interests since the last couple of dating disasters.

Mike: Hang on ... If you say she already likes you, don't you think you should just be yourself? Don't you want to feel relaxed and take her to a place you like? That seems like the best way to have a good night out with her.
Peter: Yeah! Sounds great! I've been meaning to take her to my favorite comic book store.
Mike: Well ... that's one way to look at it!
